title: hnRNPK condensates facilitate enhancer-promoter looping and RNA polymerase II recruitment.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Europe PMC: no PMCID, no full text, no supplement, no NCBI links (PubMed elink to GEO/SRA/BioProject returned nothing; Zenodo DOI search empty). GSA-Human HRA010002 (Genome Sequence Archive for Human, China) landing page says 'Open access', BioProject PRJCA034737. Listed its HTTPS download directory: 43 run folders (HRR...), each holding only paired raw FASTQ (sequencing reads) files plus a small XML; two sampled runs had 5.6+5.5 GB and 16.1+16.5 GB of FASTQ. No processed peak, loop or count files. The companion GSA accession CRA021979 sits behind a browser security check and its download server refused the connection.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Data availability (via web search snippet of the Nature page): CUT&Tag, Pol II ChIP-seq, chromatin RNA-seq, TT-seq, HiChIP, RIC-seq and CLIP-seq deposited in CRA021979 and HRA010002; public ENCODE histone ChIP-seq and eCLIP reused. Assay list, cell types (HeLa, mouse fibroblasts) and any supplementary tables were not seen; the paper is paywalled.

a1_downloadable.note: HRA010002 is open access over HTTPS/FTP (checked directory listing); CRA021979 not reachable from here.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Checked files: only raw FASTQ. Any label (hnRNPK binding sites, enhancer-promoter loops, Pol II occupancy) would have to be built by aligning reads and calling peaks/loops; no processed table is deposited and the supplement is not retrievable.

a3_inputs_present.note: No feature table exists; inputs would come from genome coordinates after running alignment pipelines on raw reads.

a4_units_stated.note: No processed values deposited, so no units to check.

a5_enough_rows.note: Number of called peaks or loops unknown without reprocessing; not verifiable.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: Hundreds of GB of FASTQ (43 runs, sampled runs 11-33 GB each)
a6_fits_laptop.note: Raw sequencing data well beyond the 50 MB rule and laptop processing; HiChIP/RIC-seq processing needs a cluster.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Paper text not available; cannot compare run counts to the paper's sample list.

a8_label_provenance.note: Labels would trace to physical measurements (CLIP, ChIP, HiChIP), not model outputs, if they were constructed.

existing_models.name: SPEID (enhancer-promoter interaction from sequence, Quantitative Biology 2019)
existing_models.score_and_split: Reported effective across six cell types; split and numbers not retrieved.

existing_models.name: Reformer (RNA-protein binding at single-base resolution, trained on 225 eCLIP sets for 155 RBPs)

backbone.name: Nucleotide Transformer / DNABERT-2 or RNA-FM for sequence windows (hypothetical)
backbone.hardware: Would need reprocessed peaks first; not assessed.

integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Does hnRNPK binding on nascent enhancer/promoter RNA predict which enhancer-promoter pairs loop, across cell types?

controls.external_validation: ENCODE eCLIP for hnRNPK in HepG2/K562 could serve, but not checked

honest_claim_h3: Not reached: no processed labelled table exists to make any claim from.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use DNA/RNA sequence around enhancers and promoters to predict where hnRNPK binds and which enhancer-promoter pairs form loops.
plain_idea.train_on: Sequence windows at candidate enhancers and promoters; number of examples unknown because only raw reads are deposited.
plain_idea.predict: hnRNPK binding (from CLIP-seq, a crosslinking assay that maps protein-RNA contacts) or loop presence (from HiChIP, a protein-anchored 3D contact assay), both requiring reprocessing of raw reads.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Would test whether an RNA-binding protein's footprint explains 3D genome contacts, but only after a large sequencing-reprocessing effort.

more_or_better_data.why: Single lab, a few cell types; existing enhancer-promoter predictors use multi-cell-type Hi-C/ChIA-PET data, and Reformer already uses 225 eCLIP sets.

confidence_score.why: Replicate structure unknown without the paper's sample table.

models_beatable.why: SPEID (2019) is old, but newer pretrained predictors (EPIPDLF 2025) exist; their splits were not retrieved.

guaranteed_improvement.why: No processed data to add to any baseline; measurements would need reprocessing, and evaluation splits differ.

ml_idea: Predict hnRNPK binding or enhancer-promoter looping from sequence; blocked because only raw FASTQ is deposited.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated: building any label requires aligning hundreds of GB of raw reads and calling peaks/loops, a cluster job.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Already done: listed HRA010002 and found only raw FASTQ (sampled runs 11-33 GB each), no processed tables.

verdict_reason: Fails A2 and A6: the only accessible deposit (GSA-Human HRA010002) holds raw FASTQ alone across 43 runs, sampled at 11-33 GB each. Any label would have to be built by reprocessing reads, the paper and supplement are paywalled, and the companion archive CRA021979 was unreachable.
